title: Concrete Pump Vertical vs Horizontal Conveying Distance
seoTitle: Vertical vs Horizontal Concrete Pump Distance | Pinjin
description: Do not add H and V into one number. Xingtai tables print pairs, sometimes split by aggregate. Electric 80 lists 900 m / 300 m; Electric 60 fine-stone lists 200 m / 600 m. ACI notes extra pressure for vertical pipe.
primaryKeyword: concrete pump vertical vs horizontal distance

answerBlock.what: Pinjin conveying distance is a printed horizontal / vertical pair for a stated mix, not a single ‘max metres’ slogan. Electric 80 lists 900 m / 300 m (2 cm aggregate). Electric 60 lists fine-stone 200 m / 600 m, 13 mm 150 m / 450 m, 24 mm 100 m / 300 m. Diesel 120 lists 150 m / 500 m. ACI 304.2R notes that vertical pumping adds pressure (industry figure: about one bar per 4 m of rise) and that hose is not equal to the same length of steel pipe.
answerBlock.who: Engineers converting floors to metres, or buyers who copied one marketplace ‘max distance’ onto the wrong Pinjin row.
factors: The H/V pair on that model page, not another model’s pair
Which aggregate row (fine-stone / 13 mm / 24 mm) if the table splits them
Vertical rise and elbows add equivalent length — we do not invent a factory loss formula beyond the printed pair
Hose versus steel (see the hose vs pipe page)

faqs.question: Can I add horizontal and vertical metres together to pick a pump?
faqs.answer: No. Use the pair printed on the model page. Electric 15 is 60–80 m horizontal and 15–20 m vertical as two figures. Electric 80 is 900 m / 300 m. We do not publish a factory formula that converts a job into one equivalent metre and then invents a SKU.

faqs.question: Why is Electric 80’s vertical 300 m while Electric 60 fine-stone lists 600 m?
faqs.answer: They are different printed rows. Electric 80: 110 kW, 60 m³/h, 40 MPa, 900 m / 300 m, ≤2 cm. Electric 60: 90 kW, 40 m³/h, 35 MPa, fine-stone 200 m / 600 m. Do not merge the 900 m horizontal onto the 600 m vertical. Match the mix to the row that actually prints it.

faqs.question: Does vertical pipe need more pressure than the same length of horizontal pipe?
faqs.answer: ACI 304.2R cites an industry estimating note that vertical pumping adds about one bar per 4 m of rise, and that hose is not 1:1 with steel. Pinjin does not republish a guaranteed site pressure from that note. We only confirm whether your stated H and V sit inside a printed pair.
